learnerStatement: Simulated learner. This review finds problems; it is not evidence that anyone learned.
learnerBoundary: Everyday numeracy, simple charts, comparing numbers and familiar household objects; no domain-specific theory assumed.

observations.prediction: Selected the west sea and locked the destination prediction for rain 55 km from the west coast and 150 km from the east.
observations.exploration: Triggered rain at the original dot, rain west of the ridge, then basin coloring. The final view showed the original dot's winding eastward path and a second westward path, separated by a divide near the west coast. Coloring reported 80% drains east.
observations.reveal: The reveal corrected the destination to east, explained water follows slope rather than nearest coast, and connected the second west-side drop and 80% basin to the ridge as a drainage divide.
observations.visual: Inspected the inline dark 1257 by 936 screenshot after coloring. A narrow dark west basin marked 20% and broad blue east basin marked 80% were separated by a jagged white divide. A salmon route crossed east from the original dot; a dashed white route ran west from the second spot. Distance labels remained visible.
observations.isolation: No-history evaluation preview banner present. Visible trust count ignored.
observations.reference: Own CUA tab 543884163 snapshots and inspected inline screenshot; no screenshot file saved.

prediction.reason: The question targets nearest-coast intuition with concrete distances.
prediction.evidence: Selected west despite the longer east drainage route.

interaction.reason: Two drops and basin coloring connect local paths to a regional division.
interaction.evidence: Drops on opposite sides reached opposite seas and coloring exposed unequal basin areas.

payoff.reason: The reveal explains the observed direction and the divide.
payoff.evidence: It ties the 150 km route and 80% east area to the ridge.

clarity.reason: The colored basins and routes make the destination distinction readable.
clarity.evidence: The final map labels both percentages and the divide.

transfer.reason: The watershed principle is generalized within the same island without a new application.
transfer.evidence: No fresh terrain or practical runoff case is developed.

accessibility.evidence: Keyboard, focus, contrast audit, phone, zoom/reflow and motion unknown.

surprise.reason: The nearer sea receives none of the original drop despite being much closer.
surprise.evidence: The original dot drains 150 km east rather than 55 km west.

visualExplanation.reason: The basin overlay converts separate routes into an understandable landscape rule.
visualExplanation.evidence: The divide encloses a narrow west drainage area and broad east area.

playfulness.reason: Rain triggers invite exploration but only two locations are available.
playfulness.evidence: Two preset drops and a coloring button drive the sequence.

practicalValue.reason: It explains why drainage cannot be inferred from coast distance.
practicalValue.evidence: The reveal identifies slope and divides as the relevant features.

depth.reason: The lesson connects local flow to whole-area drainage shares.
depth.evidence: Two paths are followed by 20/80 basin coloring.

complexity.reason: Following paths on a simple invented map requires little notation and a familiar downhill rule.
complexity.conceptualDemand: Low to moderate: distinguish geometric nearness from a downhill route.
complexity.conceptualChallenge: A ridge partitions where water can flow despite nearby alternative coasts.
complexity.prerequisiteNovelty: Drainage divide and basin are introduced.
complexity.notationRepresentationBurden: Low: simple map, distances and area percentages.

whyCool: A line near one coast can decide the destination of rain across most of an island.
caveat: The invented map routes all surface water to a sea and does not model infiltration, storage or changing terrain.
missingEvidence: Transient drop animation was not separately inspected; the final paths were inspected.
No fresh rainfall location was selectable.
